title: The Christmas Tree Ship: The Rouse Simmons, 1912

sources.what: 'failed to arrive in Chicago Harbor on schedule'; 'flying its flag at half-mast'; '3,000-5,000 Christmas trees'; count 'as high as 23'; widow Barbara and daughters 'continued the family's Christmas tree business'; found 1971; Capt. Herman E. Schuenemann, 'Captain Santa'

'Late in the afternoon on Nov. 22'; 'never arrived at Chicago'; 'flying a distress flag five miles offshore'; 'estimated 16 crew and passengers'; 'Christmas trees washed up along the coastline' for years; wallet 'near Two Rivers, Wis.' (1923); wreck at 165 feet
sources.who: Wisconsin Shipwrecks (Wisconsin Historical Society / Sea Grant)

sources.what: 'got underway from Thompson on 22 November 1912'; 'spotted a schooner at 2:50 P.M. on Saturday, 23 November 1912 flying an ensign at half mast'; 'Local fisherman reported pulling up evergreen trees in their nets'; found 1971 by Kent Bellrichard

beats.text: For years after the ship went down, Christmas trees kept washing ashore.
beats.label: LAKE MICHIGAN, 1912
beats.credit: Wisconsin Historical Society; Wisconsin Marine Historical Society

beats.text: November 22, 1912. The schooner Rouse Simmons left Thompson, Michigan, bound for Chicago, her deck piled high with Christmas trees.
beats.label: NOVEMBER 22, 1912

beats.text: Her captain was Herman Schuenemann. People called him Captain Santa.
beats.label: "CAPTAIN SANTA"

beats.text: The next afternoon, a life-saving crew at Kewaunee, Wisconsin, spotted a schooner flying a distress signal. A rescue boat from Two Rivers found nothing.
beats.label: NOVEMBER 23, 1912

beats.text: Fishermen pulled evergreens up in their nets. And in the 1920s, a fishing net brought up the captain's wallet.
beats.label: IN THE NETS

beats.text: His widow and daughters kept selling Christmas trees in Chicago. And since 2000, a Coast Guard cutter has carried trees to the city every year.
beats.label: THE TRADITION
